newsitem.title: USA: Columbia expects most USG gas cuts back Tues.
newsitem.headline: Columbia expects most USG gas cuts back Tues.

text.p: Columbia Gulf Transmission, a unit of Columbia Gas System Inc, said Tuesday it expected most natural gas shut in as a precaution against Tropical Storm Josephine to be back on line later today.
"As of now, all but 200 million (cubic feet per day) is back and that's expected back at any time," a company spokesman said.
The spokesman said about 600 mmcfd total had been cut by producers from late Friday through Monday as they evacuated platforms in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico ahead of the storm.
He said the cuts did not affect customers.

Josephine was downgraded overnight from a tropical storm, as it dissipated when it moved across Florida. At 0500 EDT, the storm was located 50 miles southeast of Savannah, Ga., moving east-northeast at 25 mph, with winds of about 50 mph.
There were no reports of major damage or injuries.
